description: Connected scatter plot of the share of Australian households with pets against the number of pet-owning households, Animal Medicines Australia surveys from 2016 to 2025. Based on the Vega connected scatter plot example.

title.description: The big heading and the smaller line under it. On a phone the words are split into shorter lines.

text.signal: 'Pet-owning households and ownership rate over time'

subtitle.signal: 'Each point is an Animal Medicines Australia survey; follow the path from 2016 to 2025'

usermeta.readMe: Vega ignores this box. It holds plain-language notes for the parts of the chart that cannot carry their own "description".
usermeta.config: Default look for both axes: no axis line, no tick marks, and set text sizes and gaps for the numbers and axis titles.

scales.x: Turns the share of homes with a pet (58% to 76%) into a left-to-right position.
scales.y: Turns the number of pet-owning homes (in millions) into an up-and-down position. It starts at 5.4 million on a computer and 4.9 million on a phone.
scales.align: Turns a label side ("left", "right", "above", "aboveleft") into how the text lines up against its dot.
scales.baseline: Turns a label side into whether the text sits beside or above its dot.
scales.dx: Turns a label side into how far the text moves left or right away from its dot.
scales.dy: Turns a label side into how far the text moves up away from its dot.

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.
usermeta.readingNote: As Australia gains households, pet-owning homes can increase even when the share with a pet falls.
usermeta.clickSelection: story-interactions.js pins a main-mark selection in pinnedKey and clears it on an empty-space click. Species hues, quantitative colours, symbol areas and plotted positions retain their meanings.

signals.name: extraHeight
signals.description: Extra plot height the page can add so a paired card ends level with its partner. This chart is not in a pair, so it stays 0.

signals.name: height
signals.description: How tall the plot is: 380 pixels (plus extraHeight, which is 0 here).

signals.name: colorAccent
signals.description: Colour: the blue highlight colour, used for the one thing we want you to notice. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-accent in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorHeading
signals.description: Colour: the dark blue colour of chart titles. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorMuted
signals.description: Colour: the dark grey colour of small text: labels, axis words and notes. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-muted in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorSurface
signals.description: Colour: white, the colour of the card each chart sits on. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-surface in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorBorder
signals.description: Colour: light grey, used for gridlines, empty squares and places with no data. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-border in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontHeading
signals.description: Font: the fancy title font (DM Serif Display). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontBody
signals.description: Font: the plain font for all other text (Fira Sans). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-body in css/style.css.

signals.name: width
signals.description: How wide the chart is. It starts as the width of the box on the page and updates whenever the browser window is resized.

signals.name: narrow
signals.description: Below 640 pixels of available width: only the emphasised 2019 label keeps its values, the bottom axis has fewer numbers and the left axis starts lower.

signals.name: hoverYear
signals.description: Temporary hover focus; mouseout restores the default emphasis.

signals.name: pinnedKey
signals.description: Main-mark selection pinned by a click. Empty chart space clears it; the loader preserves it across responsive redraws.

signals.name: focusYear
signals.description: Pinned selection takes precedence over temporary hover.

signals.name: colorPage
signals.description: Plain annotation background supplied by --color-page in css/style.css.

signals.name: readingWidth
signals.description: Keep the reading note compact, with a narrower column on phones.

signals.name: readingLines
signals.update: wrapChartText(['As Australia gains households, pet-owning homes can', 'increase even when the share with a pet falls.'], readingWidth, 12, fontBody)
signals.description: Wrap source lines that each have fewer than sixty characters; font measurement can only shorten each line.

signals.name: colorBaseline
signals.description: Dark sandy baseline marks, supplied by --color-baseline in css/style.css.

data.name: trend
data.description: The four surveys (2016, 2019, 2022, 2025): the share of homes with a pet and the number of pet-owning homes in millions.

transform.description: Choose which side of its dot each year's label goes on, so labels do not bump into the line.
Write the label's second line, for example "73% · 7.7 million".
Emphasise 2019: pet-owning household counts rose while the ownership percentage fell.
Join observations in chronological order, independently of input row order.

data.name: readingAnchor
data.description: Anchor the reading note to the 2019 observation; all four surveys are always visible.

axes.description: The bottom axis: share of homes with at least one pet, in percent, with upright gridlines. Fewer numbers on a phone.
axes.title: Households with at least one pet

axes.description: The left axis: pet-owning homes in millions, with flat gridlines.
axes.title: Pet-owning households (millions)

marks.description: Sandy line joins the surveys chronologically, from 2016 to 2025.
Sandy survey dots; 2019 is blue by default. Hover or click transfers blue emphasis to another survey, and clearing a pin restores the 2019 emphasis.

tooltip.signal: "In " + (datum.year) + ", " + (format(datum.household_ownership_pct, ',')) + "% of Australian households owned pets, or about " + (format(datum.pet_households_millions_rounded, '.1f')) + " million households. The survey included " + (format(datum.sample_n, ',.0f')) + " adults."

stroke.signal: (focusYear !== null ? datum.year === focusYear : datum.highlight) ? colorAccent : colorBaseline

fill.signal: (focusYear !== null ? datum.year === focusYear : datum.highlight) ? colorAccent : colorBaseline

marks.name: surveyPoints

marks.description: Year labels accompany the points. On phones, only the emphasised 2019 point keeps its values; its label sits above-right to avoid the left edge. The 2022 label sits below-right, clear of the reading note and connecting path.

dy.signal: datum.year === 2022 ? 12 : narrow && datum.highlight ? -24 : (narrow && !datum.highlight) ? ((datum.side === 'aboveleft' || datum.side === 'above') ? -10 : 0) : scale('dy', datum.side)

tooltip.signal: "In " + (datum.year) + ", " + (format(datum.household_ownership_pct, ',')) + "% of Australian households owned pets, or about " + (format(datum.pet_households_millions_rounded, '.1f')) + " million households. The survey included " + (format(datum.sample_n, ',.0f')) + " adults."

fill.signal: (focusYear !== null ? datum.year === focusYear : datum.highlight) ? colorAccent : colorMuted

marks.name: surveyLabels
trendReadingNote
marks.description: Left-aligned reading note above the 2019 point. Lines contain no more than sixty characters and wrap to the available column.

x.signal: clamp(scale('x', datum.household_ownership_pct) - readingWidth / 2, 12, max(12, width - readingWidth - 12))

marks.name: trendReadingBackground
marks.description: Plain annotation background follows the text bounds without borders or shadows.
